osteoporosis.reason: Loaded spinal flexion and forward bending stress vertebrae.
osteoporosis.alternative: Use neutral spine core stabilizers and supine leg slides.

osteoporosis.reason: Inversion and end-range spinal loading can compress weak bones.
osteoporosis.alternative: Replace with gentle pelvic tilts in supine.

osteoporosis.reason: Rounded spine rolling applies repeated flexion stress.
osteoporosis.alternative: Choose supported knee folds or single-leg stretches.

osteoporosis.reason: Forward flexion with load increases vertebral compression risk.
osteoporosis.alternative: Try seated postural work with neutral spine extension.

osteoporosis.reason: High-load core lift in flexion and balance can strain the spine.
osteoporosis.alternative: Use modified supported sit-up progressions with a ball.

osteoporosis.reason: Inversion and loaded spinal articulation may compress fragile vertebrae.
osteoporosis.alternative: Choose gentle supine leg slides or pelvic tilts with neutral spine.

pregnancy.reason: Heavy abdominal flexion can stress the growing uterus and diastasis recti.
pregnancy.alternative: Move to side-lying or supported seated core work.

pregnancy.reason: Inversion and supine leg lift may be uncomfortable after mid-pregnancy.
pregnancy.alternative: Use gentle pelvic floor breathing in seated or side-lying.

pregnancy.reason: Full sit-up style lifting and balance can overwork the linea alba.
pregnancy.alternative: Focus on neutral spine posture and pelvic floor activation.

pregnancy.reason: Supported head and torso lift from supine can strain the belly and neck.
pregnancy.alternative: Use safe standing or side-lying core variations.

pregnancy.reason: Inversion and spinal compression are best avoided during pregnancy.
pregnancy.alternative: Choose side-lying stretches and gentle supported hip work.

low_back_pain.reason: Repetitive spinal flexion can aggravate a painful disc or posterior chain.
low_back_pain.alternative: Choose pelvic tilts and supported bridging with neutral spine.

low_back_pain.reason: Loaded rolling may flare low back symptoms.
low_back_pain.alternative: Use gentle seated or supine core stabilization exercises.

low_back_pain.reason: Rotation with spinal flexion can irritate a sensitive lumbar spine.
low_back_pain.alternative: Use hip-focused side-lying work and neutral spine rotation.

low_back_pain.reason: Inversion and lumbar extension can be too intense for many back conditions.
low_back_pain.alternative: Use supported bridge progressions and gentle hip lifts.

low_back_pain.reason: Spinal articulation with inversion can aggravate low back pain and neural tension.
low_back_pain.alternative: Use neutral pelvic stabilization exercises and gentle supine stretch work.

hypertension.reason: Inversion may raise blood pressure and should be avoided.
hypertension.alternative: Use seated or quadruped mobility with steady breathing.

hypertension.reason: High-effort inversion can stress the cardiovascular system.
hypertension.alternative: Choose neutral spine plank holds or seated leg work.

hypertension.reason: Breath-holding and rapid rotation may spike blood pressure.
hypertension.alternative: Use slow, controlled hip circles with relaxed breathing.

hypertension.reason: Balance inversions can feel too intense for heart concerns.
hypertension.alternative: Stay on the mat with core stability and leg lifts.

hypertension.reason: Inversion and spinal compression can elevate blood pressure in sensitive individuals.
hypertension.alternative: Choose low-lying core stabilization and gentle standing mobility.

knee_issues.reason: Deep hip lift can load knees and aggravate joint pain.
knee_issues.alternative: Use gentle pelvic tilts and supported glute bridges.

knee_issues.reason: Plank-based leg lifts place pressure on the knees and hips.
knee_issues.alternative: Work in quadruped with lifted legs or side-lying leg lifts.

knee_issues.reason: Prone leg extensions can irritate knee or hamstring tension.
knee_issues.alternative: Use seated or side-lying single-leg moves with reduced range.

knee_issues.reason: Repeated knee flexion may strain arthritic joints.
knee_issues.alternative: Choose static leg holds or gentle marching in supine.

knee_issues.reason: Reformer leg pressing can place continuous load through sensitive knees.
knee_issues.alternative: Use seated or supported legwork with small range and lighter resistance.

hip_issues.reason: Large hip circles can aggravate painful or unstable hips.
hip_issues.alternative: Use smaller leg circles or hip hinges with support.

hip_issues.reason: Extreme hip range in supine can irritate hip joints.
hip_issues.alternative: Keep legs lower and work with smaller controlled lifts.

hip_issues.reason: Wide open leg balance places strain on the hip capsule.
hip_issues.alternative: Use seated adductor and abductor control work.

hip_issues.reason: Rotational hip motion may be painful if the joint is inflamed.
hip_issues.alternative: Choose gentle supported hip pumps in supine.

hip_issues.reason: Repeated leg pressing can irritate sensitive hips due to loaded flexion and extension.
hip_issues.alternative: Work with small range and lighter resistance, or choose supine leg slides.

neck_shoulder.reason: Sustained lifted head and neck can aggravate cervical tension.
neck_shoulder.alternative: Keep the head supported while maintaining core breath.

neck_shoulder.reason: Unsupported head lift increases neck strain and shoulder tension.
neck_shoulder.alternative: Use chin-tucks and gentle supported rolling in a neutral neck.

neck_shoulder.reason: Head lift with balance can load neck and shoulder stabilizers.
neck_shoulder.alternative: Use seated supported core work and avoid full V position.

neck_shoulder.reason: Prone back extension stresses the neck and upper shoulders.
neck_shoulder.alternative: Use gentle prone lifts with hands under shoulders for support.

neck_shoulder.reason: Loading the shoulders over the bar can aggravate shoulder instability or neck tension.
neck_shoulder.alternative: Use gentle supported back extension with lower resistance.

neck_shoulder.reason: Reformer shoulder loading under an inverted spine can stress tight neck/shoulder areas.
neck_shoulder.alternative: Choose supported prone back extension or supine spine mobilization without inversion.

recent_surgery.reason: Loaded spinal flexion is often too aggressive after surgery.
recent_surgery.alternative: Focus on gentle breathing, pelvic floor, and posture support.

recent_surgery.reason: Inversion and deep articulation can be unsafe during recovery.
recent_surgery.alternative: Choose supported movements and follow professional clearance.

recent_surgery.reason: Twisting with load may stress healing tissues.
recent_surgery.alternative: Use neutral spine rotation from seated or standing positions.

recent_surgery.reason: Lateral flexion can be uncomfortable after surgery.
recent_surgery.alternative: Keep movements gentle and avoid end-range bending.

recent_surgery.reason: Inversion and deep spinal articulation are usually contraindicated after recent surgery.
recent_surgery.alternative: Use gentle supine pelvic tilts and supported spine mobilization.

arthritis.reason: Repetitive flexion may aggravate stiff joints.
arthritis.alternative: Use small spinal articulations and neutral core work.

arthritis.reason: Rotation with forward flexion can irritate arthritic joints.
arthritis.alternative: Use seated side-lying rotation with support.

arthritis.reason: Inverted hip circles may be too intense for sensitive joints.
arthritis.alternative: Choose simple hip circles with reduced range.

arthritis.reason: Rolling can feel harsh on arthritic spine or hips.
arthritis.alternative: Use supported core strengthening without dynamic rolling.

arthritis.reason: Reformer leg press work can aggravate arthritic knee or hip joints without careful load management.
arthritis.alternative: Use lighter resistance and focus on small controlled range.

arthritis.reason: Inversion and spinal compression may be uncomfortable for arthritic joints.
arthritis.alternative: Choose gentle spine mobilization without large range or inversion.

scoliosis.reason: Large spinal flexion can accentuate the curve if not controlled.
scoliosis.alternative: Use supported roll-downs with a neutral pelvis and asymmetry awareness.

scoliosis.reason: Rotation through the spine may create uneven loading in a curved spine.
scoliosis.alternative: Do gentle seated side stretches with equal attention to both sides.

scoliosis.reason: Deep asymmetric side flexion can strain a scoliotic curve.
scoliosis.alternative: Work with small side bends and keep the ribs long.

pelvic_floor_dysfunction.reason: Strong abdominal pumping and breath coordination may increase pelvic floor pressure.
pelvic_floor_dysfunction.alternative: Keep the head supported and focus on gentle pelvic floor engagement.

pelvic_floor_dysfunction.reason: Repeated hip flexion and lower abdominal engagement can irritate a weak pelvic floor.
pelvic_floor_dysfunction.alternative: Perform supported knee folds or modified marching with neutral pelvis.

pelvic_floor_dysfunction.reason: Full sit-up movement loads the pelvic floor and linea alba.
pelvic_floor_dysfunction.alternative: Use supported seated core work and avoid full V position.

diastasis_recti.reason: Strong abdominal pumping can widen the separation and increase intra-abdominal pressure.
diastasis_recti.alternative: Use supported core work with the head down and focus on transverse abdominis engagement.

diastasis_recti.reason: Loaded spinal flexion places stress on the linea alba.
diastasis_recti.alternative: Practice pelvic tilts and supported roll-downs with a neutral spine.

diastasis_recti.reason: Full V-position and abdominal lift can overstress separated abdominal muscles.
diastasis_recti.alternative: Use modified seated core work with bent knees and low lift.

diastasis_recti.reason: Combined lower ab extension and arm reach may increase pressure through the midline.
diastasis_recti.alternative: Choose heel slides and single-leg supports with minimal abdominal strain.

shoulder_instability.reason: Heavy shoulder loading over the bar may aggravate instability or impingement.
shoulder_instability.alternative: Use supported back extension with lighter resistance and stable shoulder placement.

shoulder_instability.reason: Prone extension can place excessive demand on the neck and shoulder stabilizers.
shoulder_instability.alternative: Choose gentle prone lifting with hands under shoulders for support.

shoulder_instability.reason: Repeated alternating arm lifts can overwork unstable shoulder joints.
shoulder_instability.alternative: Use lower range arm extension with more emphasis on scapular stability.

shoulder_instability.reason: Shoulder-supported bridge positions may increase discomfort if the shoulders are unstable.
shoulder_instability.alternative: Keep the upper body relaxed and work with lower bridge variations or supine glute engagement.

bursitis.reason: Large hip circles can irritate inflamed bursae around the hip or pelvis.
bursitis.alternative: Use smaller, slower leg circles with a supported pelvis.

bursitis.reason: Repetitive hip rotation may aggravate bursitis in the hip joint.
bursitis.alternative: Choose gentle supported hip pumps in a neutral range.

bursitis.reason: Prone back extension can compress already tender shoulder bursae.
bursitis.alternative: Work with supported chest lifts and avoid aggressive upper back extension.

bursitis.reason: Extended upper-body reach and loaded carriage movement may stress sensitive shoulder tissues.
bursitis.alternative: Use lighter springs and smaller arm movements while keeping the shoulders stable.

vertigo_dizziness.reason: Inversion can trigger dizziness and disorientation.
vertigo_dizziness.alternative: Choose gentle supine pelvic tilts or seated mobility instead.

vertigo_dizziness.reason: Rapid spinal rotation with legs overhead can disrupt balance.
vertigo_dizziness.alternative: Use slow hip circles with the head supported and eyes fixed.

vertigo_dizziness.reason: Inversion and sudden balance challenge may worsen vertigo.
vertigo_dizziness.alternative: Stay on the mat with supported bridge progressions and slow movement.

vertigo_dizziness.reason: Advanced inversions and balancing can provoke lightheadedness.
vertigo_dizziness.alternative: Focus on floor-based core stability and steady breath.

postpartum.reason: Loaded spinal flexion and abdominal lifting can stress a recovering postpartum core.
postpartum.alternative: Use supported pelvic tilts and gentle seated core reconnection work.

postpartum.reason: Full V-style lifting can overload the healing linea alba and pelvic floor.
postpartum.alternative: Practice supported seated core lifts with bent knees and gentle breath.

postpartum.reason: Strong abdominal extension and reach may overpressure a recovering midline.
postpartum.alternative: Choose heel slides and single-leg supports with minimal abdominal strain.

balance_issues.reason: Advanced balance work increases fall risk and instability.
balance_issues.alternative: Focus on grounded floor-based stability and slow core control.

balance_issues.reason: Inversion and high balance demand can be too challenging for unstable clients.
balance_issues.alternative: Use supported bridge progressions and low-level hip lifts.

balance_issues.reason: Legs overhead inversion can challenge balance and spatial orientation.
balance_issues.alternative: Choose seated or supine core mobility without inversion.

joint_replacement.reason: Reformer leg pressing can place too much load on a replaced knee or hip.
joint_replacement.alternative: Use lighter springs, smaller range of motion, or seated leg support.

joint_replacement.reason: Loaded knee flexion and hip movement can strain a replaced joint.
joint_replacement.alternative: Choose supported knee lifts with minimal range and controlled alignment.

joint_replacement.reason: Large hip circles may aggravate a replaced hip joint.
joint_replacement.alternative: Use smaller supported leg circles or isometric hip stability work.

foot_ankle_issues.reason: Reformer footbar work places repeated load through the ankles and forefoot.
foot_ankle_issues.alternative: Use lighter resistance and keep the feet flat with minimal plantarflexion.

foot_ankle_issues.reason: Weight-bearing through the feet and ankles can aggravate sensitive joints.
foot_ankle_issues.alternative: Choose seated or supported hamstring stretches without heavy foot load.

foot_ankle_issues.reason: Rapid lower-leg movement and pointed foot positions can irritate ankle or foot pain.
foot_ankle_issues.alternative: Use slower supine leg circles with a neutral foot position.

hypermobility_syndrome.reason: Large unsupported joint ranges can overstretch lax connective tissue in hypermobility.
hypermobility_syndrome.alternative: Use smaller curves, active stability, and keep the pelvis supported during leg circles.

hernia.reason: Loaded abdominal flexion and strain may increase intra-abdominal pressure and irritate a hernia.
hernia.alternative: Choose pelvic tilts, supine core work, and gentle breath support without heavy crunching.

parkinsons_disease.reason: Unstable balance challenges increase fall risk when motor control and reaction speed are affected.
parkinsons_disease.alternative: Use grounded, supported movement with a wide base and slow transitions.

multiple_sclerosis.reason: Sustained breath pumping and core intensity can overheat or overly fatigue someone with MS.
multiple_sclerosis.alternative: Use shorter, cooler sessions with gentle breath-based core work.

stress_incontinence.reason: Strong abdominal extension and pelvic pressure may exacerbate leaking or pelvic floor symptoms.
stress_incontinence.alternative: Use heel slides and gentle core engagement with the pelvis stable.

disc_degeneration.reason: Repeated spinal flexion and compression can aggravate an already degenerated disc.
disc_degeneration.alternative: Choose neutral spine pelvic tilts and supported core stabilization.

radiculopathy_sciatica.reason: Deep spinal flexion can increase nerve root compression and sciatica symptoms.
radiculopathy_sciatica.alternative: Use gentle supported spinal mobility and avoid forward-bending under load.

ankylosing_spondylitis.reason: Inversion and axial compression may stress an inflamed, stiff spine and limit chest expansion.
ankylosing_spondylitis.alternative: Choose supported bridge work and gentle seated spinal mobility.

sacroiliac_dysfunction.reason: Large leg circles can create uneven pelvic shear and irritate the SI joint.
sacroiliac_dysfunction.alternative: Use small, controlled leg movements with the pelvis stabilized.

cervical_spine_dysfunction.reason: Unsupported head lifting and cervical flexion can aggravate neck dysfunction.
cervical_spine_dysfunction.alternative: Keep the head supported and use gentle core exercise without deep neck motion.

frozen_shoulder.reason: Prone back extension can aggravate a stiff, painful shoulder and restrict comfortable range.
frozen_shoulder.alternative: Use supported chest lifts with the arms light and close to the body.

rotator_cuff_injury.reason: Heavy shoulder loading and external rotation may irritate an injured rotator cuff.
rotator_cuff_injury.alternative: Choose gentle supported shoulder mobility and avoid deep load on the shoulder joint.

acromioclavicular_sprain.reason: Shoulder compression and upper-body load can worsen pain at the AC joint.
acromioclavicular_sprain.alternative: Use pelvic tilts or low bridge variations with reduced shoulder pressure.

thoracic_outlet_syndrome.reason: Sustained shoulder elevation and breath coordination can increase compression near the thoracic outlet.
thoracic_outlet_syndrome.alternative: Use gentle chest opening with arms supported and avoid overhead shoulder positions.

tennis_elbow.reason: Weight-bearing on the hands and forearms can aggravate lateral elbow tendon irritation.
tennis_elbow.alternative: Use lower-load shoulder work and avoid forceful gripping or wrist extension.

golfers_elbow.reason: Forearm loading and wrist action can strain the medial elbow in golfer’s elbow.
golfers_elbow.alternative: Choose supported upper-body work with minimal wrist or grip forcing.

nerve_compression.reason: Twisting and spinal compression can pinch a sensitive nerve and worsen compression symptoms.
nerve_compression.alternative: Use gentle spinal mobility with neutral alignment and avoid end-range twist.

carpal_tunnel_syndrome.reason: Wrist extension and gripping can increase pressure in the carpal tunnel.
carpal_tunnel_syndrome.alternative: Use supported core work with a neutral wrist and reduced finger grip.

cubital_tunnel_syndrome.reason: Plank-style upper-body loading can compress the ulnar nerve at the elbow.
cubital_tunnel_syndrome.alternative: Use supported core work and keep the elbow straight and free from direct pressure.

radial_nerve_issue.reason: Wrist and arm positioning under load may aggravate radial nerve symptoms if the arm is extended or compressed.
radial_nerve_issue.alternative: Use gentle core work with the wrists and elbows in neutral, pain-free positions.

ankle_sprain.reason: Unsupported balance work can stress a healing ankle and increase the risk of re-sprain.
ankle_sprain.alternative: Use seated or supported leg work with both feet grounded.

achilles_tendinopathy.reason: Reformer footbar pushing can overload the Achilles tendon with repeated plantarflexion.
achilles_tendinopathy.alternative: Use lighter resistance and avoid strong push-off through the feet.

posterior_tibialis_dysfunction.reason: High-volume footbar work may exacerbate medial ankle and arch strain.
posterior_tibialis_dysfunction.alternative: Use gentler, neutral foot positions and reduce repetitive loading through the inner foot.

tibial_stress_syndrome.reason: Repeated leg press work can aggravate shin pain and stress reactions in the tibia.
tibial_stress_syndrome.alternative: Choose lower resistance and avoid long high-volume leg sets.

plantar_fasciitis.reason: High footbar pressure and toe extension can irritate the plantar fascia.
plantar_fasciitis.alternative: Use soft, neutral foot placement and lower resistance with less toe flexion.

bunions.reason: Narrow foot positions and forefoot pressure can increase bunion discomfort.
bunions.alternative: Use wider, softer foot placement and avoid pressing directly through the big toe joint.

hip_arthroscopy.reason: Large hip circles can strain the healing hip joint and deep tissue after arthroscopy.
hip_arthroscopy.alternative: Use smaller, supported leg circles and keep the pelvis stable.

piriformis_syndrome.reason: Wide hip opening and rotation can aggravate piriformis irritation and sciatic symptoms.
piriformis_syndrome.alternative: Use gentle hip mobility with the legs closer together and the pelvis supported.

hamstring_tendinopathy.reason: Aggressive hamstring lengthening and rapid alternating leg motion can worsen tendon irritation.
hamstring_tendinopathy.alternative: Use gentle hamstring control and avoid fast, end-range leg swings.

muscle_strain.reason: Loaded posterior chain work and sustained muscle tension can aggravate an acute strain.
muscle_strain.alternative: Use gentle, supported mobility and avoid strong, resisted leg extension.

snapping_hip_syndrome.reason: Fast, large hip circles may trigger snapping and irritate the hip tissues.
snapping_hip_syndrome.alternative: Use smaller, slower hip movements with emphasis on stability.

greater_trochanteric_pain.reason: Side-lying pressure and strong lateral hip movement can aggravate greater trochanter pain.
greater_trochanteric_pain.alternative: Use gentle standing or supine hip work with less lateral load.

femoroacetabular_impingement.reason: Deep hip flexion and internal rotation can pinch the front of the hip in FAI.
femoroacetabular_impingement.alternative: Use smaller hip circles and avoid end-range flexion and rotation.

patellofemoral_pain.reason: Reformer leg press can increase compression under the kneecap and worsen anterior knee pain.
patellofemoral_pain.alternative: Use lighter resistance and keep knee alignment stable with shallow range.

iliotibial_band_syndrome.reason: Repetitive knee flexion and hip adduction may irritate the outer knee and IT band.
iliotibial_band_syndrome.alternative: Use controlled lower-leg work avoiding excessive hip adduction.

meniscus_tear.reason: Loaded knee flexion and weight-bearing can aggravate a meniscus tear.
meniscus_tear.alternative: Use gentle knee extension work with less compressive load.

ligament_injury.reason: Deep or loaded knee flexion may strain healing knee ligaments.
ligament_injury.alternative: Use controlled, supported knee work with minimal weight and a neutral alignment.

chronic_fatigue.reason: High-repetition breath and core work can worsen fatigue if pacing is too aggressive.
chronic_fatigue.alternative: Use shorter sets, gentler breath work, and allow rest breaks.

chronic_fatigue.reason: Sustained prone arm and leg lifts can be too demanding for low-energy clients.
chronic_fatigue.alternative: Choose single-limb lifts with frequent recovery pauses.

chronic_fatigue.reason: Extended plank-based leg lifts may overtax a fatigued body.
chronic_fatigue.alternative: Use supported quadruped or supine core exercises with less sustained load.

diabetes.reason: High-resistance leg work can be challenging if circulation or neuropathy is present.
diabetes.alternative: Use lighter springs and focus on smooth, controlled carriage movement.

diabetes.reason: Prolonged prone effort may fatigue the shoulders and legs quickly.
diabetes.alternative: Choose shorter duration posterior chain work with frequent rest.

diabetes.reason: Rapid alternating lower body movement can be uncomfortable if sensation is reduced.
diabetes.alternative: Use slower leg rhythms and keep the pelvis stable.

weight_concerns.reason: High core and balance demand can be difficult under added body weight.
weight_concerns.alternative: Use supported core lifts with bent knees and a lower center of gravity.

weight_concerns.reason: Inversion and rapid leg lifting may increase strain on the lower back and hips.
weight_concerns.alternative: Choose supported bridges and slower hip lifts with a neutral spine.

weight_concerns.reason: Dynamic rolling balance can be unstable and overly demanding on the joints.
weight_concerns.alternative: Focus on controlled seated or supine core work with stable foot contact.

weight_concerns.reason: Advanced balance and leg extension demand can tax joint control and stability.
weight_concerns.alternative: Use grounded stability exercises with both feet on the mat and small range movements.

respiratory.reason: Inversions and upper-body compression can make breathing difficult for people with asthma.
respiratory.alternative: Use supported chest lifts and avoid chest-compressive or breath-holding positions.

respiratory.reason: Legs-overhead position and spinal flexion can restrict the rib cage and challenge breathing.
respiratory.alternative: Choose gentle supine core work with the head and chest supported.

respiratory.reason: Rapid breath cycling and core intensity may trigger wheezing or breathlessness.
respiratory.alternative: Practice slower breath-based abdominal work with frequent rest and open chest posture.

swollen_glands.reason: Supportive head and neck lifting can aggravate tender lymph nodes in the neck.
swollen_glands.alternative: Keep the head supported and focus on gentle core activation without heavy neck motion.

swollen_glands.reason: Legs-overhead inversion may increase pressure and discomfort around swollen neck and shoulder nodes.
swollen_glands.alternative: Choose more neutral, supported supine core work with the head and neck in a comfortable position.

swollen_glands.reason: Strong rotation around the cervical spine can irritate tender lymph nodes in the neck and jaw.
swollen_glands.alternative: Use smaller seated rotations with a long spine and avoid deep turning of the head.

vision_impairment.reason: Unsupported balance poses depend on visual feedback and can increase fall risk with low vision.
vision_impairment.alternative: Use grounded, supported exercises like seated leg work and stable standing mobility.

vision_impairment.reason: Inversion and quick transitions can be difficult to judge safely when vision is impaired.
vision_impairment.alternative: Choose supported supine mobility and gentle core work with hands on stable surfaces.

hearing_impairment.reason: Exercises requiring fast verbal cues are harder to follow without reliable hearing.
hearing_impairment.alternative: Use slow, predictable movement with visual demonstration and clear gestures.

hearing_impairment.reason: Complex timing and balance in Teaser can be unsafe without visual or tactile cueing support.
hearing_impairment.alternative: Use supported seated core lifts with bent knees and steady cues.

epilepsy_seizure.reason: Inversions and rapid spinal articulations may raise the risk of a seizure-related fall.
epilepsy_seizure.alternative: Keep the spine low with supported bridge progressions and slow movement.

epilepsy_seizure.reason: Unstable balance work can be dangerous if a seizure occurs during the exercise.
epilepsy_seizure.alternative: Use stable floor-based core work and avoid unsupported balancing positions.

severe_allergy.reason: Reformer straps and props can contain latex or allergens that trigger a severe reaction.
severe_allergy.alternative: Use mat-based lower-body work with hypoallergenic props and clean equipment.

chronic_pain_syndrome.reason: Sustained core pumping can be too intense for widespread pain sensitivity and fatigue.
chronic_pain_syndrome.alternative: Practice shorter sets with the head supported and gentle breath timing.

chronic_pain_syndrome.reason: High core demand and balance requirements may flare pain in multiple regions.
chronic_pain_syndrome.alternative: Use modified seated core work with support and low lift.

skin_condition.reason: Prone extensions press the torso and can irritate inflamed or sensitive skin on the chest and abdomen.
skin_condition.alternative: Choose supported prone lifts with forearms on the mat or seated back extension work.

skin_condition.reason: Shoulder pressure from the mat or equipment can aggravate eczema, wounds, or psoriasis on the upper body.
skin_condition.alternative: Use gentle pelvic tilts and supported glute bridge variants with padding.

transplant_immunosuppression.reason: Aggressive spinal articulation and inversion can be too stressful while immune function and recovery remain delicate.
transplant_immunosuppression.alternative: Use gentle supine pelvic tilts and supported spine mobilization without inversion.

recent_hospitalization.reason: Inversion and rapid spinal movement are often too intense for someone recovering from recent hospitalization or bed rest.
recent_hospitalization.alternative: Choose supported bridge progressions and slow, controlled hip lifts.

recent_hospitalization.reason: Unsupported balance challenges increase fall risk for clients who are deconditioned after hospitalization.
recent_hospitalization.alternative: Use grounded core strength work with both feet on the mat.

pacemaker_implant.reason: Prone back extension can compress the chest and upper body near the pacemaker site.
pacemaker_implant.alternative: Choose gentle supported chest lifts with the forearms on the mat.

pacemaker_implant.reason: Heavy shoulder and chest loading may place uncomfortable pressure near a cardiac implant.
pacemaker_implant.alternative: Use lighter support and lower-range back extension movements.

substance_use_recovery.reason: Unstable balance work can be unsafe if coordination or concentration is impaired in recovery.
substance_use_recovery.alternative: Use stable, grounded Pilates exercises with clear, simple cues.

substance_use_recovery.reason: Inversion and rapid position changes may be risky if attention and body awareness are variable.
substance_use_recovery.alternative: Choose gentle supine mobility and supported core work instead.

respiratory_pulmonary.reason: Inversion and deep chest compression can worsen breathing difficulty during pulmonary flare-ups.
respiratory_pulmonary.alternative: Use supported bridge progressions or chest-open gentle seated mobility.

respiratory_pulmonary.reason: Legs overhead and spinal flexion may restrict the rib cage and trigger breathlessness.
respiratory_pulmonary.alternative: Choose supine core work with the head and chest supported.

respiratory_pulmonary.reason: Inversion and spinal compression can make breathing uncomfortable for someone with pulmonary limits.
respiratory_pulmonary.alternative: Use gentle pelvic tilts and low-lying spine articulation without inversion.

respiratory_pulmonary.reason: High-intensity breath coordination can be too demanding for compromised lung function.
respiratory_pulmonary.alternative: Practice slower breath-based abdominal work with frequent rest.

cardiovascular_disease.reason: Inversion and high exertion can spike blood pressure and strain the heart.
cardiovascular_disease.alternative: Use low-lying core work and stable bridge progressions.

cardiovascular_disease.reason: Rapid transitions and legs-overhead positioning can be stressful for a weakened cardiovascular system.
cardiovascular_disease.alternative: Choose gentle supine mobility and slow spinal articulation.

cardiovascular_disease.reason: Heavy upper-body loading may overtax heart rate response and blood pressure control.
cardiovascular_disease.alternative: Use lighter shoulder support and avoid maximal resistance.

cardiovascular_disease.reason: Sustained leg pushing may create excessive cardiovascular demand for someone with heart disease.
cardiovascular_disease.alternative: Favor slower, low-resistance leg work and monitor exertion closely.

arrhythmia_cardiac_device.reason: Deep chest compression and upper-body loading may irritate the device site or disrupt rhythm control.
arrhythmia_cardiac_device.alternative: Choose gentle supported back extension with minimal resistance.

arrhythmia_cardiac_device.reason: Prone extension and chest pressure can be uncomfortable with an implanted cardiac device.
arrhythmia_cardiac_device.alternative: Use gentle chest lifts with forearms on the mat.

arrhythmia_cardiac_device.reason: Rapid inversion and sudden effort changes may trigger an irregular heart rhythm.
arrhythmia_cardiac_device.alternative: Stay low to the mat and use controlled bridge progressions.

arrhythmia_cardiac_device.reason: Unstable balance work can be unsafe if an arrhythmia affects coordination or awareness.
arrhythmia_cardiac_device.alternative: Use grounded core stability exercises with both feet on the mat.

metabolic_endocrine.reason: Fast breath pumping and sustained core intensity can destabilize blood sugar and energy levels.
metabolic_endocrine.alternative: Use shorter sets with gentle breathing and frequent rest.

metabolic_endocrine.reason: Sustained leg pushing may create rapid metabolic demand and energy swings.
metabolic_endocrine.alternative: Choose slower, lower-resistance leg work with careful pacing.

metabolic_endocrine.reason: Dynamic full-body sequencing can be too intense when metabolic or hormonal balance is unstable.
metabolic_endocrine.alternative: Focus on slower, supported core and spinal articulation work.

metabolic_endocrine.reason: High core intensity and balance demand may overtax glucose or hormone-regulated energy systems.
metabolic_endocrine.alternative: Use supported seated core lifts with bent knees and a neutral spine.

autoimmune_inflammatory.reason: Deep back extension and prolonged upper-body loading can worsen joint or tissue inflammation.
autoimmune_inflammatory.alternative: Use gentle supported prone lifts with small range.

autoimmune_inflammatory.reason: Loaded hip lift and shoulder compression may be painful or inflammatory during a flare.
autoimmune_inflammatory.alternative: Choose pelvic tilts with a neutral spine and plenty of rest between reps.

autoimmune_inflammatory.reason: Inversion and spinal compression may aggravate systemic inflammatory symptoms.
autoimmune_inflammatory.alternative: Use supine pelvic tilts and gentle spine mobilization without inversion.

autoimmune_inflammatory.reason: Large hip motion and rotational loading can feel too intense during autoimmune inflammation.
autoimmune_inflammatory.alternative: Use smaller leg circles and support the pelvis with the hands.

immune_infectious.reason: Breath-focused core intensity can be too taxing during active infection or immune compromise.
immune_infectious.alternative: Practice gentle breath work and rest when symptoms are present.

immune_infectious.reason: Inversion and higher exertion may worsen fatigue and systemic illness symptoms.
immune_infectious.alternative: Use supported bridge progressions and reduce intensity.

immune_infectious.reason: Sustained resistance work can be overly demanding while recovering from infection.
immune_infectious.alternative: Choose low-resistance, low-impact leg work with extra rest breaks.

immune_infectious.reason: Heavy upper-body effort may be unsafe during acute illness or reduced immunity.
immune_infectious.alternative: Use gentle supported back extension and stop if symptoms worsen.

oncology_treatment.reason: Inversion and spinal compression can be poorly tolerated during active cancer treatment.
oncology_treatment.alternative: Choose gentle supine core work with the head and chest supported.

oncology_treatment.reason: High exertion and inversion may increase fatigue, bruising, or cardiovascular stress.
oncology_treatment.alternative: Use low-lying bridge progressions with controlled breathing.

oncology_treatment.reason: Prone chest compression and back extension may be too aggressive during treatment-related fatigue.
oncology_treatment.alternative: Use supported prone lifts with forearms on the mat.

oncology_treatment.reason: Inversion and deep spine articulation can be risky when blood counts or tissue tolerance are low.
oncology_treatment.alternative: Use gentle supine pelvic tilts and low-lying mobility instead.

gastrointestinal_pelvic.reason: Loaded abdominal flexion can increase intra-abdominal pressure and aggravate pelvic or GI symptoms.
gastrointestinal_pelvic.alternative: Use pelvic tilts and gentle core reconnection with a neutral spine.

gastrointestinal_pelvic.reason: Strong abdominal pumping and breath coordination may worsen pelvic floor or digestive discomfort.
gastrointestinal_pelvic.alternative: Practice slower core work with less abdominal compression.

gastrointestinal_pelvic.reason: Combined lower ab extension and arm reach may place excessive strain on the pelvic floor and abdomen.
gastrointestinal_pelvic.alternative: Use heel slides and single-leg supports with minimal pressure.

gastrointestinal_pelvic.reason: High core lift and balance demand can increase pelvic pressure and abdominal discomfort.
gastrointestinal_pelvic.alternative: Use supported seated core work with bent knees and a gentle lift.

neurological_disorder.reason: Unstable balance work may increase fall risk if coordination or sensation is affected.
neurological_disorder.alternative: Use grounded core stability exercises with a wide base of support.

neurological_disorder.reason: Inversion and fast position changes can be challenging for clients with neurological coordination issues.
neurological_disorder.alternative: Choose slow, supported spinal mobility and avoid overhead leg positions.

neurological_disorder.reason: Large leg circles require control and proprioception that may be impaired in neurological conditions.
neurological_disorder.alternative: Use smaller supported leg circles or single-leg lifts with the pelvis stabilized.

neurological_disorder.reason: High balance and coordination demand can be unsafe if motor control is inconsistent.
neurological_disorder.alternative: Use supported seated core lifts with bent knees and a stable base.

mental_cognitive.reason: Complex balance poses can be unsafe if concentration, memory, or processing speed are affected.
mental_cognitive.alternative: Use simple, grounded exercises with clear, predictable cues.

mental_cognitive.reason: Dynamic sequencing and quick transitions may overwhelm someone with cognitive or mental-health concerns.
mental_cognitive.alternative: Choose slower, more linear exercises with one movement at a time.

mental_cognitive.reason: Fast rotation and coordination can be difficult to follow safely with cognitive or emotional symptoms.
mental_cognitive.alternative: Use gentle seated or supine rotation with clear, paced instruction.

mental_cognitive.reason: High complexity and balance demand may be too much when mental focus or stress tolerance are low.
mental_cognitive.alternative: Use supported seated core work with simple, steady movement.

other.reason: This condition is not specifically listed; choose gentle, supported work and consult a qualified clinician before attempting high-risk movement.
other.alternative: Use grounded Pilates with a stable base, low load, and clear instruction.

perimenopause_menopause.reason: Inversion may trigger vasomotor symptoms and elevate blood pressure during hormonal changes.
perimenopause_menopause.alternative: Choose gentle supine core work with the head and chest supported.

perimenopause_menopause.reason: High-effort inversion is unsuitable during hormonal cardiovascular changes and potential bone density reduction.
perimenopause_menopause.alternative: Use supported bridge progressions and gentle hip lifts with a neutral spine.

perimenopause_menopause.reason: Sustained high-intensity breath work may be uncomfortable during hot flashes or cardiovascular sensitivity.
perimenopause_menopause.alternative: Practice slower, breath-led abdominal work with shorter sets and open chest posture.

perimenopause_menopause.reason: Balance inversion can challenge blood pressure stability and coordination changes associated with perimenopause.
perimenopause_menopause.alternative: Use grounded stability exercises with both feet on the mat and small range movements.

stroke_recovery.reason: Loaded spinal flexion with bilateral pulling is unsafe with hemiplegia or asymmetric weakness.
stroke_recovery.alternative: Focus on gentle breathing, supported pelvic tilts, and unilateral leg slides.

stroke_recovery.reason: High-demand balance and bilateral coordination are unsafe in early stroke recovery.
stroke_recovery.alternative: Use supported seated core work with bent knees and grounded feet.

stroke_recovery.reason: Full balance inversion requires bilateral coordination that is typically unavailable after stroke.
stroke_recovery.alternative: Choose grounded core stability exercises with a wide base of support.

stroke_recovery.reason: Rotation under load can stress recovering motor pathways and challenge spastic or weak musculature.
stroke_recovery.alternative: Use gentle seated rotation with supported arms and slow, controlled movement.

stroke_recovery.reason: Plank demands bilateral shoulder and leg stability that is usually unavailable after stroke.
stroke_recovery.alternative: Work in a supported side-lying or seated position with one limb at a time.

long_covid.reason: Sustained aerobic effort can trigger post-exertional malaise in long COVID clients.
long_covid.alternative: Use shorter, gentler breath-based core work with frequent rest breaks.

long_covid.reason: Peak exertion exercise is dangerous with post-viral fatigue and energy envelope constraints.
long_covid.alternative: Use supported seated core activation with minimal load and slow pacing.

long_covid.reason: High-intensity inversion is unsafe during energy-limited post-viral recovery.
long_covid.alternative: Choose gentle supine bridging with slow transitions and rest between repetitions.

long_covid.reason: Dynamic high-effort prone exercise can trigger post-exertional symptom relapse.
long_covid.alternative: Use a gentle prone forearm lift or sphinx position with minimal effort.

long_covid.reason: Sustained prone arm and leg lifting may exhaust a long COVID client well within normal limits.
long_covid.alternative: Choose single-limb lifts with full rest between repetitions and stop at first sign of fatigue.

hip_labral_tear.reason: Large hip circles place shear stress on the labrum and may worsen tearing.
hip_labral_tear.alternative: Use very small, supported leg circles and keep the pelvis completely stable.

hip_labral_tear.reason: Wide hip opening and balance can impinge an already torn labrum.
hip_labral_tear.alternative: Use gentle seated adductor work with legs closer together.

hip_labral_tear.reason: Rotational hip loading stresses the labral tissue and risks further tearing.
hip_labral_tear.alternative: Use smaller hip movements with strict stability and avoid end-range rotation.

hip_labral_tear.reason: Extreme hip range in flexion and extension compresses and shears the labrum.
hip_labral_tear.alternative: Use gentle hip hinge work and avoid end-range hip positions.

hip_labral_tear.reason: Rapid alternating hip flexion can irritate the labral tear and increase pain.
hip_labral_tear.alternative: Use slow, controlled leg lowering with a small range and neutral pelvis.

wrist_conditions.reason: Full body weight is loaded through the wrists in the plank position.
wrist_conditions.alternative: Use forearm plank or modify to a seated leg lift to offload the wrist.

wrist_conditions.reason: Loaded wrist extension directly aggravates fractures, sprains, and tendinopathies.
wrist_conditions.alternative: Use wall push-ups or forearm-supported positions to remove wrist load.

wrist_conditions.reason: Prone push-up positioning places significant body weight through the wrists.
wrist_conditions.alternative: Use a sphinx or forearm-supported prone position to avoid wrist loading.

wrist_conditions.reason: Side plank weight-bearing loads the wrist into extension and lateral compression.
wrist_conditions.alternative: Use a forearm side plank or roll the wrist off the mat with a fist position.

wrist_conditions.reason: Sustained wrist extension under body weight can worsen any wrist injury or condition.
wrist_conditions.alternative: Use a forearm plank as a direct substitute to achieve core work without wrist load.

lymphedema.reason: Dynamic overhead arm movement can increase lymphatic pressure and worsen swelling in the affected limb.
lymphedema.alternative: Use a gentle prone forearm lift with arms supported and avoid overhead reach.

lymphedema.reason: Repeated resisted arm loading can exacerbate lymphedema and impair lymphatic drainage.
lymphedema.alternative: Use gentle, rhythmic arm movements below shoulder height with no resistance.

lymphedema.reason: Pulling resistance with the arms may worsen lymphatic flow and increase swelling.
lymphedema.alternative: Use gentle supported arm mobility without resistance and keep the limb slightly elevated.

lymphedema.reason: Overhead pushing against resistance stresses the affected lymph nodes and vessels.
lymphedema.alternative: Use a gentle reach with no resistance and keep the arm below the shoulder when possible.

lymphedema.reason: Arm squeezing or overhead pressing can increase venous and lymphatic pressure in affected limbs.
lymphedema.alternative: Focus on gentle, rhythmic lower-body or core work while resting the affected arm.
